papers.title: Radical scavenging gelatin methacrylamide based bioink formulation for three dimensional bioprinting of parenchymal liver construct

llm.relevance_to_user: 与AI生物打印方向无关，本论文聚焦于生物墨水配方优化，未涉及任何AI或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI or machine learning into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is purely a biomaterial formulation study.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种具有自由基清除能力的生物墨水，用于构建肝实质组织。
summary_zh.method: 制备甲基丙烯酰胺明胶基生物墨水，并优化其自由基清除性能。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印出具有肝实质结构的3D构建体，细胞活力良好。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞培养和打印结构表征验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a bioink with radical scavenging capacity for fabricating parenchymal liver constructs via 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Gelatin methacrylamide-based bioink was formulated and optimized for radical scavenging activity and printability.
summary_en.result: 3D bioprinted liver constructs with preserved cell viability and structural integrity were achieved.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through in vitro cell culture assays and characterization of printed structures.

papers.title: Surgical Treatment of Bone Sarcoma.
papers.abstract: Bone sarcomas are rare primary malignant mesenchymal bone tumors. The three main entities are osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and Ewing sarcoma. While prognosis has improved for affected patients over the past decades, bone sarcomas are still critical conditions that require an interdisciplinary diagnostic and therapeutic approach. While radiotherapy plays a role especially in Ewing sarcoma and chemotherapy in Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma, surgery remains the main pillar of treatment in all three entities. After complete tumor resection, the created bone defects need to be reconstructed. Possible strategies are implantation of allografts or autografts including vascularized bone grafts (e.g., of the fibula). Around the knee joint, rotationplasty can be performed or, as an alternative, the implantation of (expandable) megaprostheses can be performed. Challenges still associated with the implantation of foreign materials are aseptic loosening and infection. Future improvements may come with advances in 3D printing of individualized resection blades/implants, thus also securing safe tumor resection margins while at the same time shortening the required surgical time. Faster osseointegration and lower infection rates may possibly be achieved through more elaborate implant surface structures.

summary_en.motivation: This review summarizes current surgical treatment strategies for bone sarcoma, highlighting the potential of 3D printing.
summary_en.method: The paper reviews allograft, autograft, megaprosthesis, and rotationplasty options.
summary_en.result: 3D-printed individualized implants may improve resection accuracy and osseointegration.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; it is a narrative review.
